description.narrative:
The Government of South Africa and the United Nations adopted the South Africa United Nations Sustainable Development Cooperation Framework (2020-2025) in 2020. Subsequent to the adoption of the UNSDCF, the UN in close collaboration with Government and the Social Partners formulated and validated the UNSDCF Joint Work Plan (2020-2021) Work Plan that integrates an activity that addresses a Direct Request adopted by the CEACR in 2015 on South Africa's implementation of the Equal Remuneration Convention, 1951 (C100). The following activity under outcome 1.2 and output 1.2.1 of the Joint Work Plan reads as follows; • Facilitate capacity development for the national partners in the use of appropriate data and methodologies to identify, measure and effectively address labour market inequalities in terms of gender participation, access to employment, services and financial resources, pay gaps (i.e., unequal remuneration for work of equal value) as well as leadership positions.
The ILO provided technical input in the drafting of the Common Country Analysis (CCA) and made an input to the text relating to the Gender Pay Gap in South Africa and challenges and technical inputs in the section relating to Progress on SDG 5 & 8 as they relate to issues on gender inequality and the pay gap.
The ILO also participated in the drafting of the UNSDCF that drew upon issues flagged in the CCA on gender inequality, and the gender pay gap and the identification of structural and policy measures required to address such a gender pay gap. Under the 1st strategic priority of the UNSDCF focusing on Just, Inclusive and Sustainable Economic Growth, the ILO made substantive input to the theory of change to underscore the critical link between reducing persistent social and economic inequalities for women, youth and other marginalized groups with outcomes for better living and working under conditions of security and dignity.
Within the context of outcome 1.2 of the UNSDCF – the ILO participated in the development of the JWP for the Strategic Priority 1 – focusing on Just, Inclusive and Sustainable Economic Growth – where an activity under output 1.2 was formulated to reflect an issue raised in a Direct Request by the CEACR on the gender pay gap.

description.narrative: Utilizing the platform of the National Economic Development and Labour Council (NEDLAC), Workers Organizations in South Africa implemented a successful campaign towards the ratification of the Convention Concerning the elimination of Violence and Harassment in the World of Work (C190). In December 2020, Cabinet approved the submission to Parliament for the ratification of C190. And in July and September 2021, the National Assembly, and the National Council of Provinces within Parliament respectively, approved the ratification of C190. The Government is currently drafting the instrument of ratification for C190. In July 2019, the ILO facilitated a workshop to sensitize gender coordinators and gender male champions of the 3 main labour federations represented in the National Economic Development and Labour Council (NEDLAC) on provisions of C190, and on their role in promoting and reporting on the Gender Equality Conventions. The workshop sensitized the gender coordinators and male gender champions on the ILO's Standards Supervisory Mechanism, including the Comments of the ILO Supervisory Bodies regarding implementation gaps of C100, C111 and C189. During the workshop, the participants also developed an advocacy roadmap for the ratification of C190 which they committed to implement. Thereafter, a series of webinars to which the ILO provided technical input were hosted by the labour federations in April, June, August 2020 to promote awareness on C190 and to lobby for its ratification. Furthermore, towards the end of August 2020, the ILO provided coordination and technical inputs into a high-level session hosted by NEDLAC to lobby for the ratification of C190. Out of the 50 participants representing the tripartite-plus (with the community constituency) in the high level tripartite-plus session, 35 were female and 15 males. The high-level session culminated with concrete recommendations to strengthen national advocacy for the ratification of C190.
